name: Abkhazia
info: Broke away from Georgia in a 1992–93 war; recognised by Russia and a handful of others since 2008.

name: Abu Musa and the Tunbs
info: Gulf islands Iran took over in 1971 as Britain left; the UAE still claims them.

name: Abyei
admin: Sudan and South Sudan jointly (with UN peacekeepers)
info: An oil-rich area whose promised referendum on joining South Sudan never happened.

name: Aksai Chin
info: A high, almost empty plateau that China built a road across in the 1950s; fighting here was part of the 1962 Sino-Indian War.

name: Nagorno-Karabakh
info: An Armenian-populated enclave fought over since 1988; Azerbaijan retook it in September 2023 and most of its people fled to Armenia.

name: Arunachal Pradesh
info: India governs it as a state; China rejects the 1914 McMahon Line that put it in British India.

name: Azad Kashmir
info: The Pakistani-administered part of the former princely state of Kashmir, west of the Line of Control.

name: Bajo Nuevo Bank
claim: Jamaica, Nicaragua and the United States
info: A reef in the Caribbean.

name: Bara Hoti
info: A grazing plateau on the Uttarakhand–Tibet border.

name: Bassas da India
info: An atoll that is mostly under water at high tide.

name: Baikonur Cosmodrome
info: The world's first and largest spaceport, leased by Russia from Kazakhstan until 2050; not really contested, but not run by its owner.

name: Belize
info: Guatemala says an 1859 treaty with Britain was never honoured; both countries voted to take the claim to the International Court of Justice.

name: Doklam (Chumbi salient)
info: A plateau where Indian and Chinese troops faced off in 2017.

name: Northwest Bhutan's valleys
info: Pasture valleys on Bhutan's border with Tibet, under talks since 1984.

name: Bir Tawil
claim: No one: neither Egypt nor Sudan claims it
info: One of the few places on Earth claimed by no state: each country's preferred border gives it to the other.

name: Bird Island (Isla de Aves)
info: A sandbank that gives Venezuela a large sea zone in the eastern Caribbean.

name: Chagos Archipelago
info: Split from Mauritius by Britain in 1965; in 2024–25 the UK agreed to hand sovereignty to Mauritius, keeping a lease on Diego Garcia.

name: Brazilian Island
info: A river island where Brazil, Uruguay and Argentina meet.

name: Ceuta
info: A Spanish city on the African coast since 1668 (Portuguese before); Morocco claims it.

name: Rincón de Artigas
info: A strip of land between two streams each side calls the border.

name: Tigri Area (New River Triangle)
info: Forest between two rivers that each country says is the real border.

name: Crimea
info: Annexed by Russia in 2014 after a referendum most countries reject; internationally recognised as part of Ukraine.

name: Cyprus UN buffer zone
info: The 'Green Line' between the two halves of Cyprus, running through Nicosia.

name: Korean Demilitarized Zone
claim: Both Koreas claim the whole peninsula
info: A 4 km-wide strip along the 1953 armistice line; the Korean War never formally ended.

name: Demchok
info: A small sector of the Ladakh–Tibet border claimed by both.

name: Diego Garcia
info: The military base the Chagos islanders were removed for; leased back by the UK after the handover deal.

name: Dokdo / Takeshima (the Liancourt Rocks)
info: Two rocky islets in the Sea of Japan (East Sea) with a small Korean police post; Japan claims them as part of Shimane Prefecture.

name: Donetsk region (occupied part)
info: Held by Russian-backed forces since 2014 and claimed as annexed by Russia in 2022; internationally Ukrainian.

name: Doumeira
info: A border headland and island that led to clashes in 2008.

name: Dragonja River border
info: Part of the land and sea border left unsettled when Yugoslavia broke up.

name: Europa Island
info: A nature reserve island in the Mozambique Channel.

name: Falkland Islands (Malvinas)
info: British since 1833; Argentina invaded in 1982 and lost the war that followed. The islanders voted 99.8% to stay British in 2013.

name: Gaza Strip
claim: Its status is part of the Israeli–Palestinian conflict
info: Recognised as part of the State of Palestine by most UN members, but not by Israel and several Western countries.

name: Gibraltar
info: Ceded to Britain by the Treaty of Utrecht (1713); Spain wants it back, but its people voted to stay British in 1967 and 2002.

name: Gilgit-Baltistan
info: The northern part of the former princely state of Kashmir, governed by Pakistan; home to K2.

name: Glorioso Islands
info: Small islands north-west of Madagascar.

name: Golan Heights
info: Taken by Israel in the 1967 war and annexed in 1981; most countries see it as occupied Syrian land.

name: Guantánamo Bay
info: Leased to the US in 1903; since 1959 Cuba has refused the rent and wants it back.

name: Hala'ib Triangle
info: Two British-era lines (the 22nd parallel of 1899 and an administrative line of 1902) give different answers; Egypt has run it since the 1990s.

name: Hans Island
info: The 'Whisky War': for decades each side left a bottle of its own spirit on the island; in 2022 they split it down the middle.

name: Ilemi Triangle
claim: South Sudan (and Ethiopia, in the past)
info: Grazing land of the Turkana people, whose border lines were never fixed.

name: Perejil Island
info: An uninhabited islet where Moroccan soldiers landed in 2002; Spain removed them and both agreed to leave it empty.

name: Chafarinas Islands
info: Three small Spanish islands off the Moroccan coast.

name: Jammu and Kashmir
info: Part of the former princely state of Kashmir, divided by the Line of Control after the 1947–48 war; India and Pakistan both claim all of it.

name: East Jerusalem
info: Taken by Israel in 1967 and annexed; Palestinians want it as their capital, and most countries don't recognise the annexation.

name: Juan de Nova Island
info: One of France's Scattered Islands in the Mozambique Channel.

name: Junagadh
info: Its ruler joined Pakistan in 1947, but India took it over after a revolt and a referendum; Pakistan's 2020 map still claims it.

name: Islands south of the Northern Limit Line
info: Five islands near North Korea's coast, including Yeonpyeong, shelled by the North in 2010.

name: Kosovo
info: Declared independence from Serbia in 2008; recognised by about half of UN members, but not by Serbia, Russia or China.

name: Southern Kuril Islands
info: Taken by the Soviet Union in 1945; the dispute has kept Russia and Japan from signing a peace treaty for the Second World War.

name: Lawa headwaters
info: Forest between the rivers each side says is the border.

name: Luhansk region (occupied part)
info: Held by Russian-backed forces since 2014 and claimed as annexed by Russia in 2022; internationally Ukrainian.

name: Matthew and Hunter Islands
info: Two uninhabited volcanic islands.

name: Mayotte
info: Voted to stay French when the rest of the Comoros became independent in 1975; it became a French department in 2011.

name: Mbanié Island
info: The International Court of Justice ruled in 2025 that a 1900 treaty gives it to Equatorial Guinea.

name: Melilla
info: Spanish since 1497; Morocco claims it.

name: Northern Cyprus
admin: The Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus (recognised only by Turkey)
info: Divided from the south since Turkey's 1974 invasion; the UN treats it as part of the Republic of Cyprus.

name: Navassa Island
info: An uninhabited island the US claimed for its guano in 1857.

name: Kalapani (near Om Parvat)
info: Nepal says its border river is a different stream; it put the area on its official map in 2020.

name: Sabah (North Borneo)
info: The Philippines claims it as the heir of the Sultanate of Sulu; Malaysia has governed it since 1963.

name: Olivenza
info: Taken by Spain in 1801; Portugal has never formally recognised the border there.

name: Paracel Islands
info: Seized from South Vietnam by China in 1974.

name: Peñón de Alhucemas
info: A small Spanish island off Al Hoceima.

name: Peñón de Vélez de la Gomera
info: A rocky Spanish outpost joined to the Moroccan coast by a sandbar.

name: Senkaku / Diaoyu Islands
info: Uninhabited islands near Taiwan; claims grew after oil was suspected nearby in 1969, and Chinese ships patrol close by.

name: Rockall
claim: Ireland, Denmark (Faroe Islands) and Iceland (its seabed)
info: A bare granite rock in the North Atlantic; the dispute is really about fishing and the seabed around it.

name: South Georgia
info: A sub-Antarctic island of penguins and old whaling stations.

name: South Sandwich Islands
info: Uninhabited volcanic islands.

name: Samdu Valleys
info: Small valleys on the Uttarakhand–Tibet border.

name: Sapodilla Cayes
info: Small cays at the end of the Belize Barrier Reef.

name: Scarborough Shoal
info: A reef off Luzon that China took control of after a standoff in 2012; a 2016 tribunal ruled against China's claim.

name: Serranilla Bank
claim: Honduras, Nicaragua and the United States
info: A reef in the Caribbean.

name: Shaksgam Valley
info: Ceded to China by Pakistan in a 1963 border agreement; India says it was never Pakistan's to give.

name: Shebaa Farms
info: A small strip on the slopes of Mount Hermon; Lebanon says it's Lebanese, the UN treats it as Syrian land held by Israel.

name: Siachen Glacier
info: The world's highest battlefield: Indian and Pakistani troops have faced each other on the glacier since 1984.

name: Somaliland
info: A former British protectorate that declared independence from Somalia in 1991; it has its own government, army and currency but hardly any recognition.

name: South Ossetia
info: Recognised by Russia after the 2008 Russia–Georgia war; most countries see it as part of Georgia.

name: Southern Patagonian Ice Field
info: The last unmarked stretch of the Chile–Argentina border, left 'to be surveyed' by a 1998 agreement.

name: Spratly Islands
admin: Shared: China, Vietnam, the Philippines, Malaysia and Taiwan each hold some
claim: China, Taiwan, Vietnam, Malaysia, the Philippines and Brunei
info: Hundreds of reefs over rich fishing grounds; China has built artificial islands with runways on several.

name: Swains Island
info: A small atoll that Tokelauans see as part of their islands.

name: Taiwan
info: Governed separately since the Chinese Civil War ended in 1949; recognised by only about a dozen countries, but self-governing and democratic.

name: Tiran and Sanafir
info: Islands at the mouth of the Gulf of Aqaba that Egypt agreed in 2016 to hand to Saudi Arabia.

name: Tirpani Valleys
info: Valleys on the Himachal Pradesh–Tibet border.

name: Transnistria
info: A strip along the Dniester that broke away from Moldova after a 1992 war; no UN member recognises it.

name: Tromelin Island
info: A tiny island known for the slaves marooned on it for 15 years after a shipwreck in 1761.

name: UNDOF zone
info: A buffer zone between Israeli and Syrian forces on the Golan, patrolled by the UN since 1974.

name: Western Sahara
admin: Morocco (about 80%) and the Sahrawi Republic (the east)
claim: Morocco and the Polisario Front's Sahrawi Republic
info: A former Spanish colony; Morocco holds most of it behind a long sand wall, and the UN lists it as a non-self-governing territory.

name: Wake Island
info: A US airbase atoll that the Marshallese call Enen-kio.

name: West Bank
admin: Israel and the Palestinian Authority (in parts)
info: Occupied by Israel since 1967; the Palestinian Authority governs some towns. Most UN members recognise it as part of Palestine.

name: Guayana Esequiba
info: About two-thirds of Guyana, awarded to British Guiana in 1899; Venezuela reasserted its claim in a 2023 referendum. The International Court of Justice is hearing the case.

name: Vukovar Island
info: A Danube island; the river has moved since the old border was drawn.

name: Šarengrad Island
info: A Danube island; the river has moved since the old border was drawn.
